```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The question is about getting a paying customer within 90 days, so willingness to pay matters most. B's brief shows that its target payers already pay $49-$99/mo for this category, with sourced TherapyNotes ($69/mo) and SimplePractice pricing. A's brief admits that no competitor charges money at all.",
    "B's demand evidence comes from actual payers complaining about price. Therapists call SimplePractice 'overkill' and its pricing 'criminal,' and a third-party aggregation says 'really expensive for what it offers.' That points to a price-sensitive segment that could be pulled away with a cheaper, narrower offer. A's demand quotes come from builders' own launch threads and include an explicit counter-signal ('downright immoral').",
    "A's monetization evidence is negative. Every listed competitor is free or donation-supported, and Fakespot, backed by Mozilla, shut down in 2025. The brief reads this as a sign that the category struggles to monetize even at scale. A paid tier would have to beat free alternatives that are already installed.",
    "B is a B2B expense purchase, and only one therapist has to convert to meet the 90-day bar. The brief frames A as consumer self-pay at ~$3-5/mo against free options, and gives no evidence that any user has paid.",
    "B carries real risks, but they look like costs and delays rather than missing demand. The brief cites $8k-$25k for year-one HIPAA compliance, BAAs, and a $500/mo minimum for Capterra listings. A's core problem, whether anyone will pay at all, is unanswered and points the wrong way."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's price hypothesis of ~$3-5/mo is anchored to GPTZero's $10-15/mo individual AI-detection tier, which is a different product for a different buyer. It is also anchored to a 'typical consumer extension subscription' of ~$4.99/mo, which has no source. Nothing in the brief shows that any reader of Reddit or review sites has paid, or said they would pay, for this kind of filter.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B has its own gaps. TheraSoft and TheraFocus pricing has no source, the $29 SimplePractice tier comes only from third-party claims, and the brief concedes that switching interest flows toward full EHRs rather than stripped-down tools. The HIPAA cost and the ongoing BA obligations could realistically push the first sale past 90 days. B is chosen mainly because A shows essentially no evidence of willingness to pay, not because B's path to a first sale is well demonstrated."
}
```
